A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 27 pages of v3 and 28 pages of v4 support comparison of the text, equations, figures, tables and references. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original sampling-strategy experiments on Gaussian data, persistence diagrams, ShapeNet and MNIST, including convergence plots and numerical clustering results.

after.justification: Section 4 retains these original experiments and their reported outcomes, including Figures 4.1, 4.2 and 4.5 and Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: The sampling procedures described in Section 3 are unchanged, including Monte Carlo, orthonormal sampling, mapped QMC/RQMC sequences, Riesz and Fibonacci configurations, spherical sliced Wasserstein sampling and spherical-harmonic control variates.

E1.justification: Both versions use Gaussian data in dimensions 2, 3, 5, 10, 20 and 50; twelve persistence-diagram ensembles; ShapeNet lamp, plane and bed point clouds; and MNIST. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 3 and the corresponding plot legends retain the same comparator membership within each experiment. Tables 4 and 5 also retain their respective four-method and five-method comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 4 retains the same projection budgets, Gaussian reference estimates using 10^8 projections, dataset sample sizes and dimensionality-reduction procedures. MDS, t-SNE, NMI and ARI remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The exact-distance sanity check in Remark 9, runtime and scalability analyses in Remarks 10–11, and persistence-diagram noise illustration in Figure 4.3 are retained. No new ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis appears.

E5.justification: Table 5 retains the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting. The confidence-interval discussion is also unchanged, with no added or revised experimental run counts, seeds or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The curves in Figures 4.1, 4.2 and 4.5 and all scores in Tables 4–5 are unchanged. For example, Halton's MNIST MDS NMI remains 0.91 ± 0.1. The reported qualitative findings also match.

T1.justification: The definitions, Propositions 1–6, proofs and convergence bounds are retained. Differences in extracted mathematical delimiters reflect font encoding and typesetting, not revised mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: a practical comparison of sampling strategies, regularity results, theoretical guarantees and dimension-dependent recommendations.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same explanations of convergence plateaus, dimensionality effects, theoretical limitations and sampling-cost tradeoffs. The applicability boundaries and practical recommendations are unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same implementation and repository links, library choices and parameter disclosures, including the Riesz and spherical sliced Wasserstein optimization settings. No technical or reproducibility information is added.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and research positioning are unchanged. Section 2.1 replaces an unresolved citation marker with Kolouri et al. (2018), which was already cited and included in v3's bibliography; this repairs a reference rather than introducing new related work.

P1.justification: v4 adds funding acknowledgments and publication/review metadata, adjusts an author affiliation and repairs the unresolved citation in Section 2.1. The scientific prose and section sequence remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adopts journal typography, running headers and a stacked author layout, with reflow and relocation of existing figures and tables. The graphical designs, plotted content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 repairs the unresolved citation in Section 2.1 and adds funding acknowledgments, modestly improving attribution and disclosure. These are limited editorial gains; the theory, experimental evidence and scientific conclusions remain unchanged.
